title: HyperStudy perception track bundle, v0.1
description: Root: manifest.json. Layer files validate against #/$defs/layer/<name>. Conventions in schema/README.md.

filename.description: Name of the source file when the bundle was made; a hint only.

source.description: How the bundle was made, e.g. 'pipeline run' or 'converted from bake-off run'.

assets.description: Small images under assets/ (person, face-track and object crops), referenced by relative path from layers.

box.description: [x, y, w, h] in source pixels

id.description: Model name, e.g. 'facebook/sam3' or 'LR-ASD TalkSet finetune'.

faces_detail.description: layers/faces_detail.json, the faces layer's side file (its detail.file): py-feat's output per face track sample, keyed by the layer's track ids, one entry per sample of that track in order.

au_names.description: The order of each sample's au.

emotion_names.description: The order of each sample's emo.

angles.description: Units and sign convention of head pose and gaze.

lmk.description: 68 landmarks: all x, then all y, in source pixels.

faces_mesh.description: layers/faces_mesh.json, the faces layer's mesh side file (its mesh.file): py-feat's 478-point 2D face mesh per face track sample, keyed by the layer's track ids, one entry per sample of that track in order. Large; readers fetch it only when they draw the mesh.

layout.description: The order of each sample's xy.

xy.description: 478 points: all x, then all y, in source pixels, rounded to integers.

faces_embeddings.description: layers/faces_embeddings.json, the faces layer's embeddings side file (its embeddings.file): the 512-d ArcFace identity embedding (InsightFace w600k_r50 weights, via py-feat Detectorv2) per face track sample, keyed by the layer's track ids, one entry per sample of that track in order; the vectors the layer's people and person_pairs were computed from. Identity data, and research-only (academic-only) weights, as for the faces layer.

normalised.description: Whether each v is L2-normalised. py-feat's ArcFace output is not (false): normalise before taking cosine distances.

v.description: The embedding, rounded to 4 decimal places.

transcript_diarization.description: layers/transcript_diarization.json, the transcript layer's raw side file (raw.diarization): what the speaker diarization pipeline (pyannote speaker-diarization-community-1) returned, of which the layer keeps each word's and utterance's voice. Its turns are what the voices were assigned from: a word takes the voice whose turns overlap it longest (summed over that voice's turns; a tie goes to the earlier turn), an utterance its words' most common voice. Times are unrounded (pyannote's frame grid: a turn covers the frames whose middle is in [start, end)), so the turns give exactly the layer's voices.

voices.description: Every speaker the pipeline found, as voice ids (voice:<its label>), in its order (the order of its speaker embeddings); a voice no word was assigned to is here but not in the layer's voices.

turns.description: Speaker turns in the pipeline's order (by start); turns of two voices overlap where both speak.

exclusive_turns.description: The pipeline's exclusive diarization: turns of at most one voice at a time (where turns overlap, one voice's), its version for aligning a transcript. The layer does not use them.

transcript_voice_embeddings.description: layers/transcript_voice_embeddings.json, the transcript layer's raw side file (raw.voice_embeddings): the diarization pipeline's speaker embedding per voice, the centroid (VBx responsibilities as weights) of the 256-d WeSpeaker ResNet34 embeddings of that voice's clustered speech, keyed by the voice ids of transcript_diarization's voices, in their order. Identity data (a voiceprint).

normalised.description: Whether each embedding is L2-normalised. pyannote's centroids are not (false): normalise before taking cosine distances.

oneOf.description: The embedding, rounded to 4 decimal places.
A voice the pipeline has no centroid for (it pads that row with zeros).

prosody_speakers.description: layers/prosody_speakers.json, a raw side file of the prosody layer (raw.speakers): the per-speaker pitch analysis behind the layer's semitones, and the 20 Hz contour in Hz. Pitch is Praat's To Pitch (ac) run twice: at first_pass_hz over the clip, then per speaker with a floor and ceiling of range_factors times the 35th and 65th percentiles of the first pass's voiced frames in that speaker's words (or first_pass_hz for a speaker with under min_voiced_frames of them). Semitones are 12 log2(f0 / median_hz), median_hz as stored (to 0.1 Hz). Speakers are the layer's names (contour.speakers).

settings.description: The analysis settings (pitch step, first-pass range, range factors, final-movement window and threshold, pause minimum, intensity minimum pitch, contour step, word cap, prominence).

range_source.description: speaker (from their first-pass frames) or default (too little voiced speech).

median_hz.description: Median second-pass F0 over the speaker's words, to 0.1 Hz: the semitones' reference. Null with no voiced frame in their words.

voiced_s.description: Seconds of voiced second-pass frames in their words.

f0_hz.description: Per bin, the median second-pass F0 (Hz, to 0.1) of the speaker whose utterance covers it; the layer's f0_st is it in semitones re that speaker's median_hz.

jumps.description: 10 ms steps between two voiced frames in the speaker's words, and how many jump more than an octave.

prosody_emotion.description: layers/prosody_emotion.json, a raw side file of the prosody layer (raw.emotion): the speech emotion model's (the Odyssey 2024 baseline's) raw output per utterance, which the layer keeps to 6 places under emotion.dimensional_odyssey, and the samples of decode's audio it read (from the utterance's start to its analysed end, the words capped at 1.2 s each), normalised as input_norm says.

outputs.description: The order of values: arousal, dominance, valence.

min_samples.description: A clip shorter than this has no output (null values; the layer's emotion is then empty).

input_norm.description: The model's input is (x - mean) / (std + epsilon), x the samples as int16 / 32768.

oneOf.description: The float32 outputs, unrounded, in outputs order.

gaze_heatmaps.description: layers/gaze_heatmaps.parquet, the gaze layer's raw side file (raw.heatmaps): Gaze-LLE's whole output for every head, of which the layer keeps the peak, the in-frame score and the target. One row per sample of the gaze layer's tracks, in time order (the heads of one frame in the layer's track order). Each heatmap is quantised relative to its own maximum: cell = floor(255 * heat / max), so heat is in [cell, cell + 1) / 255 * max and (cell + 0.5) / 255 * max is within max / 510 of it; only the maximum is 255, so the stored map's argmax is the cell of the layer's peak. Columns are not nullable.

columns.name: face
columns.description: The face track (face:N): the gaze layer's tracks[].face.

columns.name: sample
columns.description: The sample's index in that track's samples.

columns.name: t
columns.description: The sample's time, as the layer's.

columns.name: inout
columns.description: Gaze-LLE's in-frame score in [0, 1], unrounded (the layer's in_frame is it to 3 places).

columns.name: max
columns.description: The heatmap's largest value, the scale of heat: a sigmoid's, in [0, 1] in float32 (0 only for a map that is all zeros, whose cells are all 0).

columns.name: heat
columns.description: The 64x64 heatmap over the whole frame as uint8, row-major: byte 64 * row + col is the cell whose centre is ((col + 0.5) / 64 * width, (row + 0.5) / 64 * height) in source pixels.

shots_scores.description: layers/shots_scores.parquet, the shots layer's raw side file (raw.scores): what PySceneDetect's AdaptiveDetector computed for every frame, of which the layer keeps only the cuts. One row per frame the detector scored, in order. A cut is a frame, not among the first or last window_width, with adaptive_ratio >= adaptive_threshold and content_val >= min_content_val, at least min_scene_len frames after the previous cut (or the first frame), counting frames as round(seconds between their t * frame_rate); the layer's shots start at the cuts (t to 3 places). The detector's parameters are the file's metadata under the key detector, as JSON: adaptive_threshold, min_content_val, min_scene_len (frames), window_width, weights (of the deltas in content_val), luma_only, kernel_size (of the edge dilation), frame_size (the downscaled frame it scored, [width, height]) and frame_rate. What the detector does not compute is 0: the first frame's content_val and deltas (it has no frame before it, and the detector scores it 0) and the adaptive_ratio of the first and last window_width frames (no full window around them; none can be a cut). Columns are not nullable.

columns.name: frame
columns.description: The frame's index among those the detector scored, from 0.

columns.name: t
columns.description: The frame's time in seconds, as PySceneDetect places it (its OpenCV position, to the microsecond).

columns.name: content_val
columns.description: The frame's score: the weighted mean of the deltas (weights in the metadata; by default hue, saturation and luma equally, edges not at all).

columns.name: delta_hue
columns.description: Mean absolute difference of the HSV hue channel from the frame before, in 8-bit levels.

columns.name: delta_sat
columns.description: Mean absolute difference of the HSV saturation channel from the frame before, in 8-bit levels.

columns.name: delta_lum
columns.description: Mean absolute difference of the HSV value (luma) channel from the frame before, in 8-bit levels.

columns.name: delta_edges
columns.description: Mean absolute difference of the dilated Canny edge maps (0 or 255 a pixel) from the frame before.

columns.name: adaptive_ratio
columns.description: content_val over the mean content_val of the window_width frames on each side, capped at 255 (255 when that mean is 0 and content_val >= min_content_val, 0 when the mean is 0 and it is not).

transcript_tokens.description: layers/transcript_tokens.parquet, the transcript layer's raw side file (raw.tokens): every subword token Parakeet TDT returned (parakeet-mlx 0.5.3, greedy decoding), of which the layer keeps only the words they merge into and those words' times. One row per token, in time order. A token whose text starts with a space starts a word; the others extend it, never across a sentence. Greedy decoding has no alternative hypotheses. Columns are not nullable. Per word: the word column indexes the transcript layer's words in order, each word with a token, its start the first token's and its end the last token's (validate.py checks this).

columns.name: id
columns.description: The token's id in Parakeet's 8192-token SentencePiece vocabulary.

columns.name: text
columns.description: The token's text, a leading space for SentencePiece's word boundary.

columns.name: start
columns.description: When the token was emitted, in seconds to 3 places: its encoder frame times 0.08 s.

columns.name: end
columns.description: start plus the token's duration as TDT predicts it (0 to 4 frames of 0.08 s), in seconds to 3 places. A word's start and end in the layer are its first token's start and its last token's end.

columns.name: confidence
columns.description: parakeet-mlx's confidence in [0, 1], as computed: 1 - H / ln(8193), H the entropy of the softmax over the vocabulary and the blank at the step that emitted the token. A sentence's confidence is the geometric mean of its tokens'.

columns.name: sentence
columns.description: Parakeet's sentence: it splits the tokens at . ? and ! (counting from 0).

columns.name: word
columns.description: The index in the layer's words of the word the token is part of, or -1 for a token in no word (a word that would be only spaces).

sounds_tags.description: layers/sounds_tags.parquet, the sounds layer's raw side file (raw.tags): the AudioSet taggers' scores for all 527 classes, of which the layer keeps each 1 s step's top 5 at or above 0.2 as tagger events. A row per model output: PANNs Cnn14_DecisionLevelMax's rows first, one per 0.32 s segment (its CNN pools time by 32 frames; its 100 frames/s output repeats each segment's scores, and the last segment's to the end of the soundtrack, whose frame count is the last PANNs row's end * 100), then EfficientAT mn40's, one per 1 s step [start, end), the scores of the 5 s window centred on it. Each in time order. The file's metadata lists the 527 class names under labels (JSON), in the scores' order (AudioSet's class_labels_indices). Scores are the models' float32 sigmoids, unrounded. Columns are not nullable.

columns.name: model
columns.description: panns or mn40.

columns.name: start
columns.description: Seconds: PANNs segment i starts at 0.32 * i, mn40 step i at i.

columns.name: end
columns.description: Seconds: the next row's start, but for the last PANNs segment, which ends with the soundtrack's frames (frames / 100).

columns.name: scores
columns.description: The model's score in [0, 1] for each AudioSet class, in the order of the metadata's labels.

sounds_queries.description: layers/sounds_queries.parquet, the sounds layer's raw side file (raw.queries): PE-A-Frame large's probability for each text query every 40 ms frame, of which the layer keeps the runs of frames above 0.3 as query events. A row per frame, in time order. The file's metadata lists the queries under queries (JSON), in the probabilities' order. Probabilities are the model's float32 sigmoids, unrounded. Columns are not nullable.

columns.name: start
columns.description: Seconds: frame k starts at k * 0.04.

columns.name: end
columns.description: Seconds: (k + 1) * 0.04.

columns.name: probs
columns.description: PE-A-Frame's probability in [0, 1] for each query, in the order of the metadata's queries.

bodies_scores.description: layers/bodies_scores.parquet, a raw side file of the bodies layer (raw.scores): the person detector's (YOLOX-m's) score for every sample of the layer's tracks, which the layer does not keep (it keeps the box). One row per sample, in time order, the bodies of one time in the layer's track order. The file metadata names the detector and its detector_threshold: no detection scoring at or below it is in the layer. Columns are not nullable.

columns.name: body
columns.description: The body track (body:N): the bodies layer's tracks[].id.

columns.name: sample
columns.description: The sample's index in that track's samples.

columns.name: t
columns.description: The sample's time, as the layer's.

columns.name: score
columns.description: The detector's score in (detector_threshold, 1], unrounded (float32, as the model returned it).

bodies_duplicates.description: layers/bodies_duplicates.parquet, a raw side file of the bodies layer (raw.duplicates): every detection the producer dropped as a second detection of a person, so the de-duplication can be revisited. Of two detections in one frame whose head and shoulder joints visible in both (keypoint score >= score_threshold, at least 2) lie within a median distance of duplicate_head_dist x the smaller box's sqrt(area), the higher score is kept (the file metadata holds detector, detector_threshold, duplicate_head_dist and score_threshold). One row per dropped detection, in time order then by score (highest first), naming the layer sample it duplicated. Values are float32, unrounded. Columns are not nullable.

columns.name: t
columns.description: The frame's time: the time of the sample it duplicated.

columns.name: body
columns.description: The body track (body:N) whose sample at t this detection duplicated: the first kept body, by score, within duplicate_head_dist.

columns.name: sample
columns.description: That sample's index in the track's samples.

columns.name: score
columns.description: The detector's score (at most the duplicated body's).

columns.name: dist
columns.description: The median distance between the two detections' head and shoulder joints visible in both, over the smaller box's sqrt(area): below duplicate_head_dist.

columns.name: box
columns.description: The detection's box [x, y, w, h] in source pixels.

columns.name: kpts
columns.description: RTMW's 133 keypoints for this box, in the layer's keypoint_names order, each x, y (source pixels), score (the layer's scale).

prosody_tracks.description: layers/prosody_tracks.parquet, a raw side file of the prosody layer (raw.tracks): Praat's frames (Parselmouth), of which the layer keeps per-word and per-utterance summaries and the 20 Hz contour. Rows in this order: track pitch_first_pass (every 10 ms frame of the clip, To Pitch (ac) at 75-600 Hz, the pass that sets each speaker's range), intensity (every 10 ms frame of the clip, To Intensity at 75 Hz), then per utterance in the layer's order: pitch (its speaker's second-pass frames from its start to its analysed end, both included: every frame its words', its own and its contour bins' pitch is computed from), harmonicity (To Harmonicity (cc) on its audio: hnr_db is the mean of its frames above -200) and pulses (the glottal pulses of To PointProcess (periodic, cc) on its audio, from which jitter is computed). Unrounded. Columns are not nullable.

columns.name: track
columns.description: pitch_first_pass, intensity, pitch, harmonicity or pulses.

columns.name: utt
columns.description: The utterance's number N (utt:N) for pitch, harmonicity and pulses; -1 for the clip-wide tracks.

columns.name: speaker
columns.description: The utterance's speaker, an index into the layer's contour.speakers (whose pitch track and range it is); -1 for the clip-wide tracks.

columns.name: t
columns.description: Seconds from the audio's first sample: the frame's centre, or the pulse's time.

columns.name: value
columns.description: pitch: F0 in Hz, 0 where unvoiced (Praat's); intensity: dB (Praat floors silence at -300); harmonicity: dB, -200 where Praat finds no periodicity; pulses: 0.

columns.name: strength
columns.description: pitch: the selected candidate's strength (autocorrelation); 0 for the other tracks.

prosody_captions.description: layers/prosody_captions.parquet, a raw side file of the prosody layer (raw.captions), written by the delivery captions step: per utterance, what was sent to the OpenAI API (the prompt; the snippet's audio is not kept, only its times) and what came back, raw, of which the layer keeps captions.gpt (the parsed description, tags and emphasized_words, the tagger's tags_from_text, and the costs). The file's metadata holds, as JSON under request, what every call shares: model, tagger, context_s, rate, prices_usd_per_mtok, tags (the vocabulary by group), tag_notes, instructions and tagger_instructions (the system prompts), caption_schema and tag_schema. One row per utterance, in the layer's order. Captions are sampled: a rerun gives others. Columns are not nullable.

columns.name: utt
columns.description: The utterance (utt:N).

columns.name: snippet_start
columns.description: Start of the audio sent, in seconds: the utterance's start less context_s, or 0.

columns.name: snippet_end
columns.description: End of the audio sent: its analysed end plus context_s, or the clip's end.

columns.name: prompt
columns.description: The user text sent with the audio.

columns.name: caption_model
columns.description: The model that answered the caption call, as the API names it.

columns.name: caption_finish_reason
columns.description: Its finish reason.

columns.name: caption_arguments
columns.description: Its function call's arguments, as returned: JSON with description, tags and emphasized_words.

columns.name: caption_usage
columns.description: The API's usage object for the call, as JSON (prompt, audio and completion tokens).

columns.name: tagger_model
columns.description: The model that answered the tagger call.

columns.name: tagger_finish_reason
columns.description: Its finish reason.

columns.name: tagger_content
columns.description: Its reply, as returned: JSON with tags (the layer's tags_from_text).

columns.name: tagger_usage
columns.description: The API's usage object for the call, as JSON.

faces_pyfeat.description: layers/faces_pyfeat.parquet, a raw side file of the faces layer (raw.pyfeat): what py-feat Detectorv2 returned for every track sample that neither the layer nor faces_detail, faces_mesh and faces_embeddings keep. One row per sample of the faces layer's tracks, in time order (the samples of one time in the layer's track order). Values are py-feat's float32, unrounded. Columns are not nullable; the file's metadata names the translation and blendshape entries.

columns.name: face
columns.description: The face track (face:N): the faces layer's tracks[].id.

columns.name: sample
columns.description: The sample's index in that track's samples.

columns.name: t
columns.description: The sample's time, as the layer's (frame / fps, to 3 places).

columns.name: frame
columns.description: The source frame py-feat read (0-based decode order).

columns.name: box
columns.description: RetinaFace's face box [x, y, w, h] in source pixels, unrounded (the layer's samples[].box is it to 0.1 px).

columns.name: score
columns.description: RetinaFace's detection confidence in [0, 1] (py-feat's FaceScore); tracking keeps faces scoring at least 0.9.

columns.name: translation
columns.description: The multitask model's head translation outputs [X, Y, Z] (py-feat's X, Y, Z beside its Pitch, Roll, Yaw), as py-feat returns them.

columns.name: blendshapes
columns.description: The multitask model's 52 MediaPipe/ARKit blendshape coefficients in [0, 1], in py-feat's MP_BLENDSHAPE_NAMES order (_neutral, browDownLeft, ... noseSneerRight; the file's metadata lists them).

columns.name: mesh_z
columns.description: The 478-point mesh's relative depth per point (py-feat's mesh_z_0 ... mesh_z_477, in the model's chip-normalised units); faces_mesh keeps the points' x and y.

faces_untracked.description: layers/faces_untracked.parquet, a raw side file of the faces layer (raw.untracked): every face py-feat Detectorv2 detected that is in no track, because tracking left it out (shorter side under 40 px, or detection score under 0.9), with all of py-feat's values for it, so tracking and clustering can be revisited. One row per detection, in py-feat's order (frames in time order, RetinaFace's order within a frame); a frame with no face has no row. The value columns hold what faces_detail, faces_mesh, faces_embeddings and faces_pyfeat hold for a tracked face, under faces_detail's names where it has one, as py-feat's float32, unrounded. Columns are not nullable; the file's metadata names the au, emo, translation and blendshape entries.

columns.name: frame
columns.description: The source frame py-feat read (0-based decode order).

columns.name: t
columns.description: frame / fps, to 3 places: the time a sample of this frame has in the layer.

columns.name: dropped
columns.description: Why tracking left it out: size (shorter side under 40 px), score (under 0.9), or size+score.

columns.name: box
columns.description: RetinaFace's face box [x, y, w, h] in source pixels.

columns.name: score
columns.description: RetinaFace's detection confidence in [0, 1] (at least py-feat's detection threshold, 0.5).

columns.name: lmk
columns.description: 68 landmarks in source pixels: all 68 x, then all 68 y (faces_detail's lmk).

columns.name: au
columns.description: Action units in faces_detail's au_names order (AU01 ... AU43, sorted).

columns.name: emo
columns.description: Emotion probabilities in faces_detail's emotion_names order (Neutral, Happy, Sad, Surprise, Fear, Disgust, Anger).

columns.name: va
columns.description: Valence and arousal.

columns.name: head
columns.description: Head pose [yaw, pitch, roll] in radians, in the faces layer's angles convention.

columns.name: translation
columns.description: Head translation [X, Y, Z], as faces_pyfeat's.

columns.name: gaze
columns.description: Gaze [yaw, pitch] in radians, in the faces layer's angles convention.

columns.name: embedding
columns.description: py-feat's 512-d ArcFace identity embedding, not L2-normalised (as faces_embeddings').

columns.name: mesh
columns.description: The 478-point mesh: all 478 x, then all 478 y (source pixels), then all 478 z (relative depth, as faces_pyfeat's mesh_z).

columns.name: blendshapes
columns.description: The 52 blendshape coefficients, as faces_pyfeat's.

sidePointer.description: Where one of a layer's side files is, in what format, and what it holds.

file.description: layers/<name>.<format>: a side file the manifest lists under this layer's side_files.

format.description: json: validates against #/$defs/side/<name>. parquet: Apache Parquet, columns as #/$defs/parquet/<name>.

description.description: One line: what the file holds.

raw.description: The layer's raw side files: what its model returned beyond what the layer draws, by role (e.g. heatmaps). Optional; the faces layer's detail, mesh and embeddings point at its side files the older way.

kind.description: face: a visible face track; person: a known identity not visible (trusted voice link); offscreen: an unidentified voice

angles.description: Units and sign convention of head pose and gaze.

person.description: null: not assigned to any identity cluster (the clusterer's Unknown)

linked_body.description: Ever linked to a posed body; false is a strong false-face hint.

crop.description: assets/ path of a padded crop from the track's largest detection.

mesh.description: Where the faces_mesh side file is.

embeddings.description: Where the faces_embeddings side file is.

agreement.description: For query-model events: did a tagger agree? null for tagger events.

f0_st.description: Semitones relative to each speaker's median

default_dimensional.description: The emotion_models key readers show by default.

emotion_models.description: Per emotion key: the model that wrote it.

caption_models.description: Per caption key: the model that wrote it.

speaker.description: Whose pitch range and median the utterance is measured against: a person's label (Person C), or a diarized voice (SPEAKER_00, or off-screen SPEAKER_00).

speaker_source.description: Where the speaker comes from. The pipeline: asd_face or asd_voice_link (the speakers layer's person, via LR-ASD's speaking face or the voice's link), offscreen_voice (the speakers layer predicts an off-screen voice), diarized_voice (a speaking face with no person). Bake-off bundles: hand_label, lrasd_link, ...

emotion.description: Per emotion_models key: {arousal, valence, dominance} or categorical scores.

peaks.description: Peak absolute amplitude per bin, 0-100 relative to the loudest bin.
